title: Creon and Antigone
text:
After the brothers Eteocles and Polynices killed each other in a war for the throne of Thebes, their uncle Creon became king. He decreed that Eteocles, who had defended the city, would be buried with honor, while Polynices, who had attacked it, would be left unburied for the dogs and birds. Anyone who buried him would die.

Their sister Antigone defied him. She covered her brother's body with dust and performed the rites, declaring that the unwritten laws of the gods outranked any king's decree. Creon condemned her to be shut up alive in a rocky tomb.

Creon's son Haemon, who was engaged to Antigone, pleaded with his father. He told him the city was quietly on her side, and that a wise man knows how to bend, like the trees that bend in a flood and survive, while the rigid ones are torn out by the roots. Creon called him a slave of a woman. Then the blind prophet Tiresias warned him that the gods were angry and that he would pay with his own family. Creon insulted him too, but after he left, frightened, he finally gave way.

It was too late. When he reached the tomb, Antigone had hanged herself. Haemon attacked his father, then killed himself. When the news reached the palace, Creon's wife Eurydice killed herself as well. Creon was left alone.
lesson: Firmness becomes a fault when it stops you from hearing those who love you. If everyone around you is warning you, change course before events make the decision for you.
